sources.citation: Holm, Thomas Campanius. 1834 [1702]. Description of the province of New Sweden, now called, by the English, Pennsylvania, in America. Translated by Peter S. Du Ponceau. Philadelphia: M'Carty & Davis (Memoirs of the Historical Society of Pennsylvania 3).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reprints Campanius's vocabulary and dialogues (pp. 'Vocabulary and phrases in the American language') without accent marks; no remark on stress; only the Penn quotation ('sweetness or greatness, in accent and emphasis').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page pidg1246 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Only Ethnologue reference and 'Extinct'; Glottolog 5.1 descriptive refs (from): Goddard 1995 and Goddard 1997, both grammar sketches.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. Pidgin Delaware. English Wikipedia (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No phonology or stress information; notes only that Campanius used Swedish spelling conventions, de Laet Dutch-influenced spelling, the Indian Interpreter English/Swedish-Dutch mixed spelling. Bibliography: Goddard 1977, 1997, 1999; Thomason 1980; Feister 1973.

sources.citation: Prince, J. Dyneley. 1912. An ancient New Jersey Indian jargon. American Anthropologist n.s. 14(3): 508-524.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Edition and etymological commentary of 'The Indian Interpreter' (1684). No mention of stress or accent; p.510: 'Perhaps the most interesting phonetic feature of this jargon.. is the interchange of r and l.'

sources.citation: Thomas, Gabriel. 1698. An historical and geographical account of the province and country of Pensilvania; and of West-New-Jersey in America. London: A. Baldwin.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only 'As to the manner of their Language, it is high and lofty, with a Short Sentence.' followed by the jargon dialogues; no accent marks.

sources.citation: Campanius [Holm], Johan. 1696. Lutheri Catechismus, öfwersatt på American-Virginiske språket. Stockholm: Burchardi (J. J. Genath). [ms. 1640s; ed. Thomas Campanius Holm]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement about accent or stress anywhere (preface, catechism, Vocabularium Barbaro-Virgineorum pp.135ff., Mahakuassi vocabulary). The Delaware text nonetheless carries printed acute accents on many words, verified on the page images: 'Manétto', 'nácha', 'hátte', 'Hócque, Hocquaéssung', 'Rhénus', 'Renáppi', 'chéko', 'tahóttamen' (book p.19 and p.135; PDF pp.43, 159); their meaning is never explained. The Swedish preface quotes William Penn's 1683 letter: 'I know not a Language, spoken in Europe, that hath words of more sweetness or greatness, in Accent and Emphasis, than theirs' (impressio…

sources.note: The only monograph-length philological study of the Campanius text, the one source that prints accent marks on Pidgin Delaware words; likely to discuss what the acute accents mark (Goddard 1997 warns that Holmer's transcriptions are unreliable).
